posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Hanabi's pretty cool - it's a co-operative game where you have to collectively play cards in order from 1 to 5 in each of five colours. You get three "lives" so you can't make many mistakes. The difficulty is in that you are not allowed to see your own cards, and can only communicate with others about their cards with limited information, e.g. "Those three cards are red," or "you have no fours". It's really hard, but interesting.

Having played both Dominion and Ascension a fair bit against AI on my phone, I can say that Dominion has much less theme, but less swinginess since the cards you can buy are in 10 piles of 10 rather than an ever-shifting central row, and there's only one kind of currency. I like both, but I think Dominion is the better game - many people disagree with me though!

We'll be arriving at Victoria Coach Station at 10.10, but I'm not sure if we're planning to check into our hotel right away or if we'll do that later. Probably easiest to meet at the pub?

posts.name: Mezike
posts.cooked:
I played Pompeii at my regular club a couple of days ago, it was ok and I’d certainly play it again. A light game where you position people around the town so that you can get them out as quick as possible before the volcano goes boom. The only problem with it was that one or two turns into the second phase it was obvious who was and wasn’t going to win which deflated things a bit. We still had fun trying to mess with the inevitable though. It’s a real old school Euro, and we had a lot of debate as to how it would likely be designed differently in the modern age (hidden variable VPs on the ‘people’ would have made a massive difference)
Hanabi is great fun, particularly if you have a terrible memory for hidden information like me! 7 wonders is good as it is very scalable depending on the number of players. Anybody have a copy of Love Letter? I bought one from a friend but haven’t received it yet, it’s a nice quick filler that is also scalable and I do like it a lot.
Sociable/Party games sound like the best fit for the day so I will bring Nanuk as it is another small box game that is a good laugh with a large group. I have a feeling that we will mostly be playing Sentinels and whatever Paul happens to bring with him though!

posts.name: Azqa
posts.cooked:
Silverleaf:

Having played both Dominion and Ascension a fair bit against AI on my phone, I can say that Dominion has much less theme, but less swinginess since the cards you can buy are in 10 piles of 10 rather than an ever-shifting central row, and there's only one kind of currency. I like both, but I think Dominion is the better game - many people disagree with me though!

I know this is off-topic, but I had to poke my head in here, as Dominion was my addiction just before Sentinels (though I still have three expansions of Dominion to acquire…in time) - I agree completely that Dominion is a better game, primarily because there are more options for strategy and more chances for player interaction.  Also it feels better paced unless you have more than four people playing.

If you want to try something that is very themed but has more deckbuilding options than Ascension offers, you might try Thunderstone.  It has little in the way of player interaction, unfortunately, but I found the game mechanics (darkness penalties, physical vs. magic attack, heroes, weapons, items, spells, villagers, and some more) to be more interesting in Thunderstone.  It does tend to be a bit slower than other deckbuilders though.
